The Baritone screen, redone so you never need a command. Seven pages: Go, Mine, Follow, Roam, Tools, Settings and Commands, with a search bar on every page (press /) that understands what you mean: type coordinates and Enter goes there, a place's name goes to it, "diamonds" mines them, a player's name follows them, "sprint" switches that setting.

**Mine** lists every block by its picture and real name, in groups (Favourites, Recent, Near you with how many are around, Ores, Valuable, Wood, Stone, Nether, End, Plants, Building) or by search. Ores come as families, so "Diamond (all ore)" gets the deepslate diamonds too. Pick as many kinds as you like and how many to get (16, 64, any number): it counts what you've really picked up (diamonds, raw iron) and stops by itself when you have them, showing your haul with icons as it goes. Switches for legit mining, picking up drops, exposed ores only, and a Y range.

**Follow** shows everyone in view with their face, list mark and distance, and every kind of mob by its spawn egg. **Tools** puts the rest of Baritone on buttons: go to the nearest block of any kind, up to the surface, go so far the way you're facing or to a Y level, dig a tunnel of any size, explore, farm, pick up, mark an area and dig it out, fill it, wall it or replace blocks in it, copy and paste it, build a schematic from your folder, and force-stop when it's stuck.

**Settings** has all of Baritone's settings in plain words with what each does, in groups, each with the right control (switches, − and +, blocks and items as icons with a picker, colour swatches), plus presets: Careful, Fast, Legit-looking, and Undo all my changes. **Go** has one Go per place (▾ for the rest: either dimension's spot, set as goal, copy, pin), sorting, and pins. The header shows what Baritone is doing and, when it's idle, what you did lately to do again with one click. Pointing at anything says what it does along the bottom; 1 to 7 switch pages.
